correctness.rationale: For each nonidentity scalar \(a\), the published formula makes \(U_a-I\) invertible. If \(U_a\) is scalar, inversion forces \(A+aA^*\) to be scalar. Two distinct scalar probes therefore make \((a-b)A^*\) scalar and force \(A\) itself to be scalar. Substitution \(A=\alpha I\) gives the exact fractional-linear circle map. The identity \(|1-\alpha|^2-|\alpha|^2=1-2\operatorname{Re}\alpha\) puts the positive branch in a disk parameter \(c\) and the negative branch in a disk parameter \(d\). The inverse formulas \(\alpha=c(1-\overline c)/(1-|c|^2)\) and \(\alpha=(1-\overline d)/(1-|d|^2)\) reconstruct every holomorphic or antiholomorphic disk automorphism fixing \(1\). The cases \(\alpha=0\) and \(\alpha=1\) were checked separately.

value.rationale: The scalar unitary circle is the center of the unitary group, so identifying exactly which new order automorphisms preserve it is a natural structural question. The result gives a complete classification, a two-point detection principle, and a geometric model by the full holomorphic/antiholomorphic disk stabilizer of \(1\). It also pinpoints the classical order-plus-orthogonality theorem as exactly the identity/conjugation endpoints, clarifying how much extra freedom appears when orthogonality is dropped.
